answer: Trust edges in the web decay 10% per epoch unless a new countersignature refreshes them, and a duplicate submission forfeits the edge and the stake behind it. A rotating pool picks the auditors, so a farm cannot pre-select its judges. Ten accounts that countersign each other weekly keep their edges alive but never join the wider thread, and the moment one replays an answer the cluster drops. What the design cannot do is stop a patient operator from spreading clones across small clusters; it only grows the cost with every terrace of the graph they keep warm and every kernel of work they fake.
